A four-superfile FTS table (`body` column with positions, 100 rows per superfile, one commit each) written by the engine as it stood just before slices carried their own checks: its term index has a root at layout version 6 naming slices at version 3, with tier objects and per-superfile heads, and no record of where each slice's block index ends.

The compatibility test opens it with the current reader and checks that it answers as a table without the index does, after the current writer adds a layer in the current layout beside the old ones, and after a maintenance pass. A unit test folds its old layers and checks every term comes out the same in the current layout. Regenerate only if that older layout itself must change, which it should not: the point of the fixture is that tables indexed by it keep working.
